STATUS: ANSWER
The `-l, --merge-logic` option of `bcftools annotate` sets how multiple annotation values are combined when several regions overlap one record. The rules are `first` (use the first value), `append` (keep duplicates), `append-missing` (append even missing dot values), `unique` (drop duplicates), `sum`, `avg`, `min` and `max` [bcftools_manual#h019]. `sum` and `avg` apply to numeric fields only, and the option is experimental [bcftools_manual#h019]. It is intended for BED or TAB-delimited annotation files and works only when REF and ALT or BEG and END columns are present. Multiple rules can be comma-separated or given repeatedly [bcftools_manual#h019].

STATUS: ANSWER
Two tools in the context predict variant effects. VEP (Variant Effect Predictor, based on Ensembl) determines the effects of all kinds of variants, including SNPs, indels, structural variants and CNVs [sarek_output#h060]. snpEff annotates and predicts the effects of variants on genes, such as amino acid changes [sarek_output#h059].
The VEP VCF header records the software version and the version numbers of additional databases, such as ClinVar or dbSNP, used in the VEP line. It also describes the consequence-annotation format in the INFO field [sarek_output#h060]. The snpEff VCF header records the software version and the command line used [sarek_output#h059].

STATUS: ANSWER
The context describes Oncotator as an older functional annotation tool developed by The Broad Institute [gatk_funco_tutorial#h031]. It states that Funcotator and Oncotator are fundamentally different tools with some similarities, and the author maintains that a direct comparison should not be made [gatk_funco_tutorial#h031]. Funcotator is the functional annotation tool in the core GATK toolset. It labels each variant with one of twenty-three variant classifications and annotates it from data sources such as GENCODE, dbSNP, gnomAD and COSMIC [gatk_mutect2_wdl#h002]. The context does not state explicitly which tool is newer, and the comparison tables it refers to are not included, so the specific similarities and differences are not covered.

STATUS: ANSWER
Two tools in the context check whether samples come from the same individual. NGSCheckMate uses a set of commonly heterozygous SNPs to detect sample mislabelling. Its output lists matched comparisons with correlation and a dendrogram [sarek_output#h066]. bcftools gtcheck checks sample identity: with -g, samples in the query VCF are checked against the samples in the -g file; without -g, all samples in the query file are cross-checked [bcftools_manual#h057]. Pairs can be selected with -p or -P, and --n-matches limits the output to the top matches [bcftools_manual#h059]. The discordance score counts mismatching genotypes only for GT-vs-GT matching [bcftools_manual#h057]. The context does not give a cutoff for deciding that two samples match.

STATUS: ANSWER
Run `build_docker_remote.sh` to build the GATK4 image with Google Cloud Build. This is useful if you cannot build the image locally [gatk_docker#h001]. First run `gcloud config set project <PROJECT>` with a project that has access to Google Cloud Build [gatk_docker#h001]. Then run `sudo bash build_docker_remote.sh -e ${GITHUB_TAG} -d ${STAGING_DIR}` [gatk_docker#h004]. The image is tagged `us.gcr.io/broad-dsde-methods/broad-gatk-snapshots/gatk-remote-builds:<USERNAME>-<GITHUB_TAG>-<GIT_HASH>` and uploaded to GCR [gatk_docker#h004]. For the gatkbase image, the remote script is `build_docker_base_cloud.sh <docker_image_version>` [gatk_docker#h011].

STATUS: ANSWER
In a small tutorial dataset, some annotations have insufficient data or may have no variance. The filtering options therefore have to be changed and limited to a subset of annotations [sarek_vc_sarek#h007]. The tutorial data include only 2 samples. Running VQSR on such a small dataset causes issues with some annotations, so the step is limited to fewer parameters than usual [sarek_vc_sarek#h003]. The tutorial sets the INDEL recalibrator to `-an QD -an FS -an SOR -an DP` and the SNP recalibrator to `-an QD -an MQ -an FS -an SOR` [sarek_vc_sarek#h007].

STATUS: ANSWER
vcfanno. It annotates a VCF with any number of INFO fields from any number of VCFs, using a simple configuration file that specifies the source annotation files, the fields, and how they are added to the query VCF [rare_output#h023]. By contrast, SnpSift is set up with a CSV samplesheet of annotation databases [sarek_usage#h071].

STATUS: ANSWER
The provided sources do not list the FORMAT fields that bcftools call emits per sample. They only say that the -G option requires per-sample FORMAT/QS or FORMAT/AD tags generated by bcftools mpileup with -a QS or -a AD [bcftools_manual#h023].
A plugin is run like a normal command, but its name is prefixed with `+` (or called as `bcftools plugin NAME`). Its general options come first, then a separator `--`, then the plugin-specific options: `bcftools [plugin NAME|+NAME] '[OPTIONS] FILE -- [PLUGIN OPTIONS]'` [bcftools_manual#h095]. A normal command takes `[OPTIONS] FILE`, for example `bcftools call '[OPTIONS] FILE'` [bcftools_manual#h023]. Some plugins do not accept the common options and implement their own parameters [bcftools_manual#h095]. Examples are `bcftools +counts in.vcf` and `bcftools plugin counts in.vcf` [bcftools_manual#h103].

STATUS: ANSWER
The GATK jar is located at `/gatk/gatk.jar` inside the GATK4 docker image [gatk_docker#h002]. The script that builds the GATK4 image remotely with Google Cloud Build is `build_docker_remote.sh` [gatk_docker#h001].

STATUS: ANSWER
Install git-lfs and run `git lfs install`. Then run `git lfs pull` from the root of your GATK git clone to download the large test data, which is about 5 gigabytes [gatk_readme#h025] [gatk_readme#h002].
A full git clone is required because the build needs the git-lfs files in `src/main/resources/large`. These files are packaged inside the GATK jar and used by tools at runtime, and a zipped source archive alone is not buildable [gatk_readme#h008]. The large files in `src/test/resources/large` are needed only by the test suite, not for building [gatk_readme#h008].

STATUS: ANSWER
Two thresholds check FS. For INDEL variants the threshold is FS > 200.0 [G:Threshold:FS_gt_200_indel]. For SNP variants the threshold is FS > 60.0 [G:Threshold:FS_gt_60_snp]. Both are checked by the GATK source and belong to the hard-filtering procedure HF-01 [G:Procedure:HF-01].

STATUS: ANSWER
The procedure is HF-01 (HardFiltering), which has the threshold SOR_gt_3 (SOR > 3.0 for all variant types) [G:Procedure:HF-01] [G:Threshold:SOR_gt_3]. The graph shows seven thresholds linked to HF-01: SOR_gt_3, FS_gt_200_indel, FS_gt_60_snp, MQRankSum_lt_-12.5, MQ_lt_40, QD_lt_2 and ReadPosRankSum_lt_-8 [G:Procedure:HF-01]. The sub-graph is marked as truncated with one more neighbour omitted, so the total may be eight. The provided sources do not confirm the total.
